summary: The Toronto Fire Services 2025 Annual Report provides an overview of the fire protection services provided to Toronto's residents and visitors, along with a clear and transparent reporting of outcomes and service level performance. Toronto Fire Services provides Toronto residents, visitors, and businesses with world class fire protection services, through public education, fire prevention and all-hazards emergency response services. Toronto Municipal Code Chapter 79, Fire Services, requires the Fire Chief to prepare and present an annual report to City Council. This report fulfills that requirement and provides Council with an update on fire protection service levels, service level performance, and an overview of the numerous achievements and accomplishments in 2025.
decided: City Council on July 29 and 30, 2026, adopted the following: 1. City Council request the Fire Chief and General Manager, Toronto Fire Services to analyze the financial impacts of changes to provincial legislation and/or regulations that have an impact on Fire Services workforce costs and provide a summary to the City Manager of the annual and projected ongoing impacts. 2. City Council direct the City Manager to undertake negotiations with the Province of Ontario to recover the financial impacts, as identified by the analysis undertaken in Part 1 above, to mitigate the impact of changes to provincial legislation and/or regulations on the City of Toronto budget. 3. City Council request the Fire Chief and General Manager, Toronto Fire Services, in consultation with the Executive Director, Financial Planning, the Executive Director, Corporate Real Estate Management, and the Chief Executive Officer, CreateTO, to report back in advance of the 2027 budget process with recommendations to improve fire service response times in Etobicoke, including consideration of accelerating the planned Woodbine Fire Station and Trucks and interim measures to support adequate response capacity. 4.
